classified.text: Users shall be able to browse the product catalogue by category, brand, or popularity.
Customers can search the catalogue using keywords, filters, and price ranges.
The system shall display detailed product information, including images, specifications, price, and stock availability.
A new user shall be able to register an account by providing email, password, and optional profile data.
Users shall authenticate via email/password or third‑party OAuth providers.
The application shall allow users to reset forgotten passwords through a secure token emailed link.
Customers shall manage multiple shipping addresses and payment cards within their profile.
The cart service shall enable adding, removing, and updating quantity of items in a shopping cart.
Users shall be able to view a real‑time summary of cart contents, subtotal, taxes, and estimated shipping.
At checkout, the system shall validate stock levels and reserve inventory before order creation.
Customers shall select a shipping method, apply promotional codes, and confirm the order.
The payment gateway shall process credit‑card transactions and return success or failure status to the order service.
Upon successful payment, the order service shall generate an order record and trigger the fulfillment workflow.
The system shall send order confirmation and receipt emails to the customer immediately after payment.
Users shall track the current status of each order, including processing, shipped, in‑transit, and delivered.
Customers shall view a chronological history of all past orders with details and downloadable invoices.
The catalogue service shall allow administrators to create, update, or deactivate product entries.
An administrator shall be able to adjust inventory quantities and set price discounts for selected items.
Sock Shop shall be deployed as independent Docker containers orchestrated by Kubernetes, enabling horizontal scaling of each microservice.
The platform shall achieve 99.9% availability measured on a monthly basis, with automatic failover across multiple zones.
All inter‑service communication shall be encrypted using TLS 1.3, and data at rest shall be encrypted with AES‑256.
The system shall enforce role‑based access control (RBAC) so that only authorized personnel can perform administrative actions.
Observability shall be provided through centralized logging, distributed tracing, and metrics collection for each microservice.
The application shall respond to user‑initiated requests within 200 ms for 95 % of calls under normal load.
Autoscaling policies shall adjust the number of pod replicas based on CPU utilization and request latency thresholds.
The CI/CD pipeline shall automatically build, test, and deploy new container images without manual intervention.
